mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction companies registry (e.g., SEC, Companies House, Hong Kong Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the designated competent authority of the home registry; otherwise notarization plus consular legalization at a Canadian embassy or consulate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 6-13, 101; Business Corporations Act Regulation, Alta Reg 119/2021, Form 1; conflict-of-interest and director duties under ss. 120-121
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta (including authorized Registry Agents for online submission)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) filed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by the Alberta Business Corporations Act; shares may be issued for any lawful consideration approved by the board, and no escrow or lawyer's trust account is mandatory for the capital contribution of a non-public corporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription for 1,000 common voting shares at CAD 1.00 per share be and is hereby accepted, all in compliance with the Alberta Business Corporations Act; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be established at [Suite 700, 555 4th Avenue SW, Calgary, Alberta T2P 3E7] and the corporate records be maintained there; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Director Name] be appointed President, [Director Name] appointed Secretary, and [Director Name] appointed Treasurer, each to serve until the next annual meeting; RESOLVED FURTHER, that banking arrangements be opened with any chartered Canadian bank and signatories appointed per the attached officer schedule; and RESOLVED FURTHER, that management file all tax, municipal, and privacy registrations required for the data-pipeline and API gateway operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via an authorized NUANS search house or registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Corporate Name Search Request with three to five proposed distinctive corporate names; ensure the name includes an appropriate legal element ('Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.'); review the search report to confirm no confusingly similar existing trademarks or corporate names; reserve the selected name for a 90-day reservation period through the online Registry Agents portal.
required_dossiers: Completed Corporate Name Search / NUANS Request
List of proposed corporate names with distinctive and descriptive elements
Applicant identification (incorporator name, address, birth date)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the name as confusingly similar, file an amended reservation for a revised distinctive name within the original 90-day window; no additional reservation fee is charged for the replacement request made within the same filing session.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation and Authorizing Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and founding directors; legal counsel drafting the constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) specifying the authorized share structure (e.g., an unlimited number of common shares with no par value), restrictions on business (if any), the number of directors, and the registered office address; prepare the Consents of Directors (Form 8) and By-law No. 1; the incorporator executes the Articles and consents, with signatures witnessed and dated.
required_dossiers: Signed Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation
Executed Consents to Act as Director (Form 8)
Draft By-law No. 1 (general governance)
Officer appointment schedule (subject to post-filing board resolution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a notice of deficiency under s. 12 of the ABCA because a provision deviates from model articles, amend the Articles in accordance with the Registrar's requisition and re-submit within the stated cure period (typically 60 days) without loss of the original application priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) - online self-service portal or licensed registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation electronically through the Corporate Registry's online filing system or an authorized agent; pay the official filing fee of CAD 275 (approximately USD 215); upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation and assigns a corporate access number and file number; obtain a certified copy from the registry.
required_dossiers: Executed Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation
Receipt of official state filing fee
Corporate Name Search Report or name reservation confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried or placed in suspended status for unpaid fees or deficient particulars, remit the required fee and provide a corrected schedule within 15 business days; failure to cure within the statutory period results in withdrawal of the application and a fresh filing, preserving the original entity name priority only if the name reservation remains valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Adoption of First Board Resolution and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First board of directors named in the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting by written consent or virtual meeting immediately after issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation; approve By-law No. 1; pass the First Board Resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption, and officer appointments; issue share certificates; establish the minute book, securities register, directors' register, and officers' register; record the Journal of Resolutions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Executed organizational meeting consent or minutes
By-law No. 1
Unaudited share subscription and consideration records
Minute book and statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director's consent is missing or defective, obtain an executed Consent to Act as Director (Form 8) before the board acts; if the minute book is incomplete, prepare and back-date the organizational records using the date of incorporation, ensuring that all registers are signed by the appointed secretary within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registrations (CRA Business Number, GST/HST, Payroll, Corporate Tax Accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online (BRO) portal; Alberta Finance for provincial corporate tax coordination
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, obtain the federal Business Number (BN) by filing the RC1A or using CRA's BRO online gateway; the corporate income tax account is created automatically; register for GST/HST if the corporation's annual worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 (or voluntarily); open a payroll account if employees will be hired; Alberta corporate income tax is collected by the CRA under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act and requires no separate provincial portal registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Corporate access number and file number issued by the Alberta Corporate Registry
Registered office address and director/officer particulars
Contact details and financial institution information for direct deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA query the registration due to mismatched officer information or address, log in to My Business Account within 30 days and file an amended registration via the 'Change my business information' function; if the BN is not issued within 20 business days, contact the CRA Business Enquiries line and provide the registry extracts to expedite activation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence, Provincial Employer and Data-Privacy Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary Business Licence Centre (or applicable Alberta municipality); Workers' Compensation Board - Alberta (WCB); Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a municipal business licence application for 'Data Processing, Hosting, and Software Services' identifying the registered office or principal place of business; register as an employer with WCB Alberta if employees are engaged; confirm compliance with the Personal Information Protection Act (Alberta) for commercial data-handling if the corporation processes personal information from Alberta residents; no industrial manufacturing or environmental permit is triggered by the API gateway business.
required_dossiers: Municipal Business Licence Application (city-specific)
Certificate of Incorporation
Corporate particulars statement (officers and registered office)
Proof of any leased premises or home-based business authorization
WCB employer account registration form (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality denies the licence due to zoning or business classification, re-file under the correct NAICS code 518210 with an explanatory business plan; appeal the denial pursuant to the Municipal Government Act, RSA 2000, c M-26, s. 507; if WCB coverage is contested, supply payroll records and subcontractor agreements within the appeal period set out by the WCB Appeals Commission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over a commercial web-scraping and proxy API gateway business; the only relevant authorities are the municipal business licensing office and Alberta's consumer/data protection regulators
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempt - no manufacturing or industrial operating permit required; operations may proceed with a municipal business licence and, where applicable, a CRA GST/HST account and provincial data-privacy registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the undertaking is a purely digital service with no physical plant, no land disturbance, and no point-source emissions; therefore no registration, screening report, or full Environmental Impact Assessment is required under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or stack emission thresholds apply; if the company later leases server-hosting space exceeding small-utility scale, the tenant must comply with local electrical and electronics waste rules under the Recycling Regulation (Alberta Recycling Management Authority) for disposal of obsolete IT equipment; no other environmental discharge permits are engaged.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety certification, structural load inspection, or workplace occupation clearance is mandatory for a virtual or co-working office arrangement; if the corporation leases dedicated premises, the landlord must provide a valid occupancy permit and fire code approval under the Alberta Fire Code (NFC 2023); for any physical workstation, the corporation must comply with the Occupational Health and Safety Act (Alberta), including a general worksite hazard assessment, ergonomic equipment standards, and WCB injury-reporting protocols; no building-level industrial clearances apply to the digital API and scraping operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — national tax administration for corporate income tax, GST/HST, and payroll; authorized portal is CRA 'My Business Account' (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-individuals-gst-hst.html); Alberta corporate income tax is administered by CRA under the Federal-Provincial Tax Collection Agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign corporation carrying on business in Canada must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and a GST/HST program account (RT account) from the CRA. The non-resident applies using Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts) submitted online through the CRA's Non-Resident GST/HST registration portal or by mail to the applicable CRA tax centre. The CRA validates the foreign incorporation certificate, Canadian agent for service, and place of business in Canada before issuing the BN. Registration is mandatory when the non-resident makes taxable (non-zero-rated) supplies exceeding the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold in a calendar quarter or across four consecutive calendar quarters, or when supplying specified digital services to Canadian consumers; voluntary registration is available for zero-rated exporters to claim input tax credits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — an Alberta Business Corporation is a separate taxpayer under the Income Tax Act (Canada); no pass-through eligibility exists. It is subject to federal and Alberta provincial corporate income tax at the entity level on worldwide income; shareholders are taxed only on dividends. Territorial scope is limited by the Canada-US tax treaty for treaty-resident shareholders but the corporation remains fully resident if incorporated or centrally managed and controlled in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not offer a check-the-box election. Relevant statutory elections include: (i) non-resident corporation's section 216 election to file a return for Canadian rental income on a net basis; (ii) treaty-protected income election under subsection 115(1); (iii) GST/HST Quick Method (Form GST74) for suppliers with annual taxable supplies up to CAD 400,000; (iv) GST/HST Simplified Method for input tax credits; (v) joint election for closely related corporations (Form GST25) to treat certain supplies as being for nil consideration; and (vi) hybrid mismatch rules under Income Tax Act sections 18.2 and 18.21 that disallow deductions for hybrid mismatch outcomes, consistent with OECD BEPS Action 2.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) — Alberta applies only the 5% federal GST because the province did not harmonize its sales tax; no provincial retail sales tax exists in Alberta.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — small-supplier threshold measured over a single calendar quarter or four consecutive calendar quarters. Non-resident suppliers of 'specified digital services' (including API access, data feeds, and software automation) are deemed to make supplies in Canada and must register with the CRA once gross revenue from Canadian consumers exceeds CAD 30,000 in a 12-month period; after registration, GST at 5% is chargeable on business-to-consumer supplies, while business-to-business supply chains may be zero-rated under the non-resident B2B rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not require real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based government pre-clearance of invoices. The CRA mandates electronic filing of GST/HST returns (GST/HST NETFILE or EDI) for all registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1,500,000, for all non-resident registrants, and for registrants using a third-party intermediary. The Pan-Canadian PEPPOL e-invoicing framework is voluntary and currently limited to business-to-government transactions; commercial B2B export invoices may be issued electronically and stored digitally, but must be produced on request within CRA retention periods.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Excise Tax Act, Schedule VI, Part V: (i) section 7 zero-rates services supplied to a non-resident person who is not registered for GST/HST, except services performed in Canada in respect of real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance; (ii) section 21 zero-rates supplies of intangible personal property (data, software licenses, API subscriptions) to such non-residents. For the subject web-scraping/proxy API gateway, exports to foreign enterprise customers that are non-residents, unregistered for GST/HST, and consuming the data pipeline wholly outside Canada are zero-rated. Domestic Canadian sales or sales to GST/HST-registered non-residents are taxable at 5%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A) / Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) — applicable to physical goods, not digital services
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill with Customs cargo control number — used only where hardware or media is physically exported
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/ACH confirmation evidencing receipt of export consideration in the corporate account
Export contract, commercial invoice, and statement of work identifying the non-resident customer and offshore consumption
Digital delivery log and payment gateway settlement report (Stripe/USDC) evidencing the supply made and fee received
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess zero-rated exports within the standard 4-year limitation period, extended to 10 years for misrepresentation or fraudulent omission. If the non-resident status or offshore consumption is unsupported, the supply is recharacterized as taxable at 5%. Penalties include: (i) failure to collect/remit GST — 5% of net tax plus 10% on repeat failures; (ii) false statements or omissions — 5% to 10% of the tax amount; (iii) gross negligence penalty under Excise Tax Act section 285 — up to 50% of the tax sought; (iv) daily compound interest at prescribed rates; (v) criminal prosecution for fraud with fines up to CAD 200,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years. Exporters must retain all substantiation for at least six years from the end of the reporting period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with foreign exchange policy and prudential supervision administered by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and anti-money-laundering transaction reporting enforcement by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility under IMF Article VIII. There is no exchange-control licensing or profit-remittance approval. Dividends, interest, royalties, and management fees may be paid to non-residents without Bank of Canada authorization, but are subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (Canada) at 25%, subject to treaty reduction to 5% or 15% in typical circumstances. The only practical hurdle is the legal and beneficial-ownership documentation required by the payor bank to substantiate treaty relief.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Canada. Exporters of software, data-pipeline, or API services are free to invoice in foreign currency, retain the receipts in CAD or foreign-currency accounts, or use proceeds to settle foreign payables. Record-keeping obligations under Income Tax Act subsection 230(4) remain applicable, and any wire or cash transaction of CAD 10,000 or more is reportable to FINTRAC as a large-value transaction record.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating account (CAD/USD multi-currency) with capital-escrow sub-ledger capability
Operating account (CAD/USD) and USD clearing account
Operating account plus dedicated trust/escrow account for pre-revenue capital
Operating account (CAD/USD) and cross-border trade settlement account
Operating account (CAD) with US-dollar correspondent clearing account
Operating account (CAD) for local treasury and Payments Canada direct clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low as a primary liquidity rail. Offshore fintech EMIs and digital cross-border banking platforms (e.g., Mercury, Airwallex, Wise Business) are not Canadian Schedule I banks and cannot directly clear through Payments Canada. A foreign EMI is viable only as an auxiliary foreign-currency collection or disbursement vehicle if it holds a FINTRAC money-services-business registration or acts exclusively as a payment facilitator with settlement into a Canadian chartered bank account. An unlicensed foreign EMI that transmits funds or maintains a Canadian payment account on behalf of an Alberta corporation may itself require registration under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. The recommended structure is to use Stripe as a payment facilitator for card/USDC settlement into a Canadian operating account and to restrict EMI accounts to USD/EUR trade receipts where delivery into Canada is impractical.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian federal and Alberta corporate law do not require directors to attend an Alberta registry office in person; however, Schedule I bank KYC policies frequently impose a physical presence or a live-video identity attestation for at least one account signatory. For a non-resident-owned Alberta business corporation, the most realistic onboarding path is for one director, officer, or authorized Canadian legal counsel to attend an in-person branch appointment in Calgary or Edmonton with certified corporate records. Remote account opening is statutorily permissible under FINTRAC individual identity-verification rules, but a medium-risk web-scraping/API merchant with non-resident directors will generally be escalated to enhanced due diligence, making a physical or virtual due-diligence interview a de facto condition precedent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and beneficial owners with no Canadian nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and certified status Certificate from Alberta Corporate Registry; register of directors; beneficial-ownership attestation; passport-level government-issued ID for each director/UBO; tax-residency certificates and mailing addresses; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth letters from the remitting foreign bank; corporate organizational chart; independent legal opinion from a Canadian law firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital from a high-risk or crypto-adjacent jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full source-of-funds transaction trail from a regulated financial institution; executed share subscription agreement; board resolution authorizing share issuance; bank reference letter; sanctions and politically-exposed-persons screening results; independent legal confirmation that no crypto chain settlement was used for direct funding; on-chain-to-fiat conversion records from a licensed Canadian crypto gateway if USDC is liquidated before wiring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Data-scraping API business model perceived as high operational or reputational risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial contracts with customers; redacted client list; technical documentation and API terms of use; privacy and data-law compliance program under PIPEDA, GDPR, and website terms; information-security policy; business-plan projections; CRA corporate income-tax filing history or pre-registration plan; Alberta registered-office utility bill; payroll evidence for any Canadian contractors; third-party data-sourcing and IP licensing agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high transaction velocity and cross-border settlement to third-party processors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Consolidated treasury and cash-flow forecast by currency; payment-processing agreements with Stripe and other gateways; daily settlement schedule with cap thresholds; written AML compliance manual; external AML risk assessment by a licensed consultant; updated corporate KYC pack on each major counterparty; confirmation that all CAD settlement funnels back to the Canadian bank account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholder equity capital should be injected by SWIFT MT103 international wire or Fedwire-equivalent channel into the Alberta corporation's Schedule I bank account in CAD or USD. The SWIFT purpose code should be CFDI (Capital Financial Direct Investment), with the OECD BPM6 direct-investment equity category 510871 cited in the remittance narrative. Banks will require the receiving account name to match the corporate account exactly. The supporting verification package must include the board resolution authorizing the share issuance, executed share subscription agreement, certificate of corporate status, register of shareholders, and source-of-funds documentation from the remitting bank. If the capital originates in USDC or other cryptocurrency, conversion to CAD must occur through a licensed Canadian crypto-to-fiat gateway before the wire; direct blockchain settlement to a corporate bank account is not a compliant clearing rail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements use the following clearing rails: (i) domestic CAD payments via Payments Canada ACSS/EFT credits or Lynx real-time rail; (ii) international supplier and vendor settlements via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 COVER through the bank's correspondent network; (iii) commercial letters of credit via the issuing bank's trade desk for large software or data-infrastructure procurement contracts; and (iv) small-value global API labour or contractor payments via licensed money-services-business payout networks or Stripe Connect, provided those payouts are denominated in local currency and remitted from the CAD treasury account. All outbound disbursements must be supported by invoices, contracts, and tax documentation sufficient for transfer-pricing and GST/HST compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts against CAD/USD and other G10 currencies with a Schedule I Canadian bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA collateral protocol.
Cross-currency swaps, including FX swap and cross-currency interest-rate swap structures, executed through a Canadian chartered bank's market-making desk.
Vanilla FX call and put options for hedges of forecasted foreign-currency collections or trade payables.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for non-CAD restricted or less-liquid currencies; CAD/foreign-currency NDFs are not a standard deliverable-market instrument and are not generally necessary because the Canadian dollar is fully convertible.
CME-listed FX futures or exchange-cleared FX swaps as short-term liquidity and hedging tools for USD exposures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 60 days of the anniversary of the corporation's incorporation date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a default notice; continued failure may lead to administrative dissolution and restoration costs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the corporation's fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the balance due, plus 1% per full month up to 12 months (aggregate 17%); interest on unpaid amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return for Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as T2: within 6 months of fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same federal enforcement regime; penalties and interest are applied to any Alberta corporate tax unpaid.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers: within 3 months after fiscal year-end if revenue under the threshold; quarterly/monthly filers have earlier fixed deadlines.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of the amount owing plus 1% per month up to 12 months; no GST/HST registration or filing triggers assessment and administrative enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares demand it, unless the corporation is exempt by unanimous shareholder consent; a corporation is generally exempt when not a reporting issuer and gross revenues are below CAD 1,000,000 and assets are below CAD 1,000,000.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public companies; Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for private corporations. This entity (private, data/PI API) qualifies for ASPE.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation required in Alberta; however, the corporation must maintain an internal Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) and update it within 15 days of any change. Shareholding transfers do not trigger a filing except for updating the ISC register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
Financial Statement and Director Meeting Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined Alberta rate 23% (federal 15% after General Rate Reduction + Alberta general 8%). A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) claiming the Small Business Deduction pays 11% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income (federal 9% + Alberta 2%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED refundable investment tax credits (35% for CCPCs on qualified R&D expenditures up to approximately CAD 3.4 million; 15% non-refundable for non-CCPCs); federal General Rate Reduction (13%) embedded in the 15% federal rate; Alberta Innovation Employment Grant (refundable credit on qualifying Alberta payroll); no Alberta capital tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta combined return) filed exclusively through CRA-approved E-file/EDI software via CRA My Business Account or an authorized tax preparer; includes the Alberta corporate tax calculation (Schedule 5 provincial schedule) under the federal-provincial Tax Collection Agreement; GIFI schedules attached electronically.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (12-month fiscal period; short taxation year for first year or on change of year-end).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return due within six months after fiscal year-end; tax balance due within two months after year-end (three months for CCPCs claiming the Small Business Deduction); non-resident corporations file within six months of year-end and remit quarterly instalments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from web scraping subscriptions, proxy/API usage fees, data licensing, and ancillary services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Convert Stripe and USDC-denominated settlements into CAD at the Bank of Canada daily exchange rate; attribute revenue to Canada only to the extent services are performed through a Canadian permanent establishment (PE).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductions: cloud infrastructure, data bandwidth, proxy network costs, legal and compliance fees, R&D wages, and third-party scraping services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow payments to non-resident related parties where Part XIII withholding tax was not remitted; apply arm's-length expense allocation in cross-border cost-sharing arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income before adjustments, reconciled with audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible fines, political contributions, and 50% of meals/entertainment; adjust unrealized crypto-asset gains or losses to the tax basis on the rebased date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying non-capital loss carryforwards, capital loss restrictions, and discretionary reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete Schedule 8 loss history; do not characterize Canada-source royalty income as capital gains to circumvent s. 212 tax; consider change-of-control rules under s. 249.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax abatement: 10% of taxable income earned in a province (Alberta allocation) reduces gross Part I federal tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents without a Canadian PE cannot claim the abatement; Canada-US DTA PE threshold rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General rate reduction: 13% federal rate reduction applied to income not eligible for the Small Business Deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CCPC status is unavailable where non-residents control the corporation; the federal 9% Small Business rate then does not apply, and the full 15% federal rate is used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta income tax at 8% general rate or 2% Small Business rate (CCPC only) on taxable income allocated to Alberta.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Alberta's apportionment formula for revenue attributable to the Alberta PE; non-residents are taxable in Alberta only on income reasonably connected to the Alberta PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-capital loss and net capital loss carryback/carryforward calculations (3 years back, 20 years forward for non-capital losses).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Change of control (s. 249) may forfeit loss carryforwards; obtain tax legal opinion before any non-resident ownership restructuring.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month of delay up to 12 additional months; repeat failures add an extra 10%; daily compound interest at the prescribed quarterly rate (approximately 9% per annum) on late instalments and unpaid balances; missing or false GIFI attracts CAD 250 per day administrative penalties (min CAD 2,500, max CAD 12,500); wilful omissions trigger gross negligence penalties of 50% of the tax under s. 163(2).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII dividend withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders (ITA s. 212(2)); DTA relief: Canada-US and Canada-UK treaties reduce the rate to 15% for portfolio holders and 5% where the recipient is a company owning at least 10% of the payer's voting shares; Canada-US treaty provides 0% for qualifying pension funds.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Step 1: obtain a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the recipient's foreign tax authority covering the dividend payment year; Step 2: deliver the TRC to the Canadian payer before payment so the payer can apply the DTA rate at source under s. 212(11); Step 3: payer files CRA Forms NR301/NR302/NR303 to substantiate treaty-reduced withholding; Step 4: if the full 25% was over-withheld, the recipient files Form NR7-R with the CRA within two calendar years of the withholding year; Step 5: maintain beneficial ownership and substantive business evidence to defeat treaty-shopping reclassification.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for software/IP and data licensing: statutory Part XIII rate 25%; treaty-reduced to 10% under Canada-US and Canada-UK DTAs; interest: statutory 25% on non-arm's-length interest payments, arm's-length interest generally exempt from Part XIII; treaty rates for related-party interest are 15% under Canada-US and 10% under Canada-UK (0% for arm's-length interest); participating-debt interest and disguised dividends remain taxable at 25%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory minimum threshold in the Income Tax Act; the CRA expects contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (local file and, where applicable, master file) where aggregate cross-border non-arm's-length transactions exceed approximately CAD 1,000,000 per taxation year; Country-by-Country Reporting is mandatory for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of CAD 750,000,000 or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no standalone Economic Substance Regulation comparable to UAE ESR; substance is enforced through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s. 245, penalty of 25% of any tax benefit), the sham and agency-PE doctrines, treaty limitation-of-benefits provisions (Canada-US DTA Art. XXIX A), thin capitalization limits (1.5:1 debt-to-equity for non-resident shareholders under s. 18(4)), and the Excessive Interest and Financing Expenses Limitation (EIFEL), which caps net interest deductions at 30% of tax EBITDA for large corporate groups.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Systematically concealing USDC/crypto subscription revenue, maintaining off-book wallets, or filing a knowingly false T2 Corporation Income Tax Return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under ITA s. 239: fines of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded plus imprisonment for up to 5 years; gross negligence penalty of 50% of understated tax under s. 163(2); CRA asset seizure, bank account freezes, and criminal referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized concealment face personal civil liability for the full deficiency, joint and several penalties, criminal fines, asset confiscation, imprisonment, and US inadmissibility or border flags restricting international travel.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing API usage fees, data licensing, or management charges to a non-resident affiliate below arm's length without contemporaneous comparable analyses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment at arm's-length prices under s. 247(2); 10% transfer pricing penalty under s. 247(3) where the taxpayer fails to make reasonable efforts; daily compound interest on reassessed amounts; risk of juridical double taxation and CRA audit referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false transfer pricing documentation may be pursued personally for the 10% penalty where they directed the mispricing; civil restitution follows corporate veil-piercing where funds were diverted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a non-resident-owned Alberta corporation with no office, employees, or management functions while channelling scraping/API subscription revenue to a tax-haven parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may ignore the entity under the sham doctrine or GAAR, reassess the foreign parent on Canadian-source income, deny treaty benefits, impose the 25% GAAR penalty, and apply Part XIV branch tax of 25% on unrelieved Canadian-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors are personally liable for unremitted source deductions and Part XIII withholding under s. 227.1; travel bans and extradition risk arise where laundering of mispriced revenue is proven; long-term disqualification from Alberta directorships is possible.
